title: Flux API Pricing 2026 — What Does a Month Cost?
summary: Flux API pricing varies by model and resolution, from $0.009 per 1K images to $0.607 per 4K. Determine which tier delivers the best value for your budget.
body_markdown:
## Costs beyond Flux list price


Those limits matter because every extra generation, upscale or re-download is billed on top of the sticker price, and each one moves your effective cost per image upward.


### Cost per usable image versus cost per image


A 50% discard rate doubles the price you pay for an image you keep, because that price is the list price divided by your keep rate.


Take a model listed at $0.048 per image. If you keep every output, you pay $0.048. Keep 70% and it's about $0.069. Keep half and it's $0.096. Keep 30% and it's $0.16, more than three times the list price.


Cutting your discard rate from 70% to 50% saves more per kept image than going from 30% to 0%.


You measure your discard rate; the vendor does not publish it. The figures in this article rest on arithmetic, and the discard rates people report are mostly anecdotal. Run a batch of your own prompts and count what you keep before you budget.


### Resolution, editing and reference-image surcharges


The bigger the output, the higher the cost, and the jump to 4K is far steeper than the steps before it.


[ImageKlein](https://imageklein.com/flux-3-image-klein-api-pricing) lists Flux 3 Image Klein at $0.008 per image at 768², $0.009 at 1K, $0.011 at 1.5K, $0.014 at 2K and $0.036 at 4K.


From 768² to 2K the price rises by $0.006, so going up several tiers costs little. The step from 2K to 4K adds $0.022, and 4K costs about 2.6 times the 2K price.


If you generate everything at 4K when most of it ends up at 2K or below, you pay that multiple on every image. Draft at a low tier and render at 4K only the keepers.


On some providers, editing and reference inputs are billed differently from plain text-to-image calls. Check whether your vendor charges for each input image, because a workflow that feeds in two references per edit is paying for more than one image per output.


Budget for that when you price the workflow.


### Flux storage, retry and rate-limit costs


Because result URLs expire, you have to download and store every image you intend to keep. That puts storage and transfer on your own bill, and it means a discarded image you want back may be gone for good.


Retries add cost twice. A failed or throttled request may still be billed, depending on the provider, and each retry is another generation counted against your discard rate above. A pipeline that retries on every error can quietly inflate the effective price.


Flux bills each retry and edit as another image, but the flow wrapped around them doesn't have to bill you again for being carefully built.


On[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) the run is the meter, not the steps inside it: a ten-step pipeline of prompt, generate, check, save and review costs the same 1 credit per flow run as the two-step shortcut it replaced.


Zapier's per-task and Make's per-module billing climb with every step added, so they tax the builder for splitting work into smaller, more reliable integrations.


Rate limits cost engineering time rather than cash. Queueing, backoff and concurrency caps have to be built and maintained, and that labour belongs in the monthly total alongside the per-image price.
